title: Car Shakes When Accelerating
summary: Common causes, likely diagnostic paths, OBD references, and repair-next steps when the car shakes under acceleration.
intro: A shake on acceleration often points to a load-related misfire, lean fuel delivery problem, or airflow fault when the engine is asked to make power. If the shake comes with hesitation, a flashing check engine light, or a stored misfire code, engine-performance diagnosis should come before guessing at parts.
common_sounds: Shudder or shake that gets worse with throttle
Stumble or bucking under moderate to heavy load
Flashing check engine light during acceleration
Loss of smooth power as RPM climbs
quick_checks: Scan for P0300 through P0304, lean-condition codes, and airflow-performance codes
Note whether the shake happens only under load or also at idle
Inspect spark plugs and coils before moving deeper into fuel or catalyst faults
Check fuel trims and fuel delivery if the shake gets worse climbing hills or under heavier throttle
Inspect intake ducting and MAF-related connections if hesitation is paired with airflow codes
common_causes: Weak fuel delivery or injector fault
Lean condition from intake or vacuum leak
Catalyst restriction or exhaust backpressure problem in some cases
diagnostic_paths: If the shake comes with a flashing MIL or clear cylinder-drop feel, start with misfire diagnosis before chasing sensors.
If the engine goes lean under load, fuel pump output and shared fuel-delivery issues move higher on the list.
If power falls off without a strong misfire but airflow data looks implausible, verify the MAF path before replacing ignition parts.

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Misfire Under Load Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use misfire counters and ignition checks first when vibration appears with throttle demand.
checks: Check P0300-family codes and freeze-frame load
Inspect plugs, coils, and coil boots
Confirm whether the shake follows a cylinder or affects multiple cylinders

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Fuel and Airflow Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: If the shake is tied to hills, highway speed, or lean trims, fuel delivery and airflow move up.
checks: Check fuel pressure or volume when power falls off
Inspect intake ducting and MAF signal plausibility

recommended_repairs.title: Spark Plug Replacement Cost
recommended_repairs.description: A strong first repair path when the shake is tied to worn plugs or load-related spark breakdown.

recommended_repairs.title: Ignition Coil Replacement Cost
recommended_repairs.description: Relevant when the shake follows a weak coil or gets noticeably worse as cylinder demand rises.

recommended_repairs.title: Fuel Pump Replacement Cost
recommended_repairs.description: A useful next path when acceleration load exposes weak pressure or volume delivery.

recommended_repairs.title: Mass Air Flow Sensor Replacement Cost
recommended_repairs.description: Worth pricing when hesitation and shake line up with biased airflow data or contamination.

recommended_repairs.title: Catalytic Converter Replacement Cost
recommended_repairs.description: Only use this path after misfire and fueling causes are checked if power loss suggests restriction.
